title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: Condition (a) as first written demands bijectivity of Ob(f), which contradicts (c): there Ob C' -> Ob C is a μ-torsor, surjective but not bijective. Grothendieck himself flags this with '[+ surjectivité ... sur les objets, quitte à préciser]'. The definition is visibly in draft state.
Items 1°)/2°) are listed in reversed order, and the definition is unfinished on this page (conditions b-d continue on p. 93). There is no mathematical error beyond the inconsistency above.
Formula (15) needs μ to act freely on the objects of the fibre. That hypothesis is stated on p. 91 and later in (c), not repeated here.

ideas.what: Fibre groupoid C'_ξ identified with the groupoid ℰ(E) built from a μ-torsor E and a central extension ℰ of μ by π: objects E, Hom(x,y) = ℰ_{y-x}
ideas.modern_name: action/translation groupoid E//ℰ; trivialized π-gerbe; groupoid of a torsor twisted by a central extension
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard groupoid/gerbe folklore (Giraud, Cohomologie non abélienne 1971, for gerbes)
ideas.where_published: related gerbe/lien formalism in Giraud and SGA; not this specific formulation

ideas.what: Π-groupoid: a groupoid with a central action π -> Aut(id_C)
ideas.modern_name: groupoid banded by a central group / π-gerbe; π-linear structure via the center of the category
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks and Esquisse discuss related groupoid formalisms; unsure about this exact notion

ideas.what: (π,μ)-fibration of groupoids subordinate to a central extension 0->π->ℰ->μ->0: a strict π-fibration with a free compatible μ-action whose fibres are governed by ℰ
ideas.modern_name: μ-equivariant central extension of groupoids / action of the 2-group (strict Picard groupoid) attached to ℰ on a π-gerbe; lifting group actions to gerbes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Breen, Laumon-Moret-Bailly style equivariant gerbes; 2-group actions (Baez et al.) – generic theory

ideas.what: Recovering the extension class from the fibres via the transitive system H_u, H_u∧H_v ≅ H_{uv} (p.93)
ideas.modern_name: classification of central extensions via multiplicative torsors (Grothendieck's own SGA7 formalism of extensions via torsors)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA 7, exposé VII, biextensions/extensions as multiplicative torsors)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a formalism of '(π,μ)-fibrations of groupoids subordinate to a central extension', apparently meant to describe fractional Dehn-twist / rotation actions of μ_n on Teichmüller groupoids with tangential base points. It is left in draft with unresolved conditions. Published work on Teichmüller groupoids and the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group (Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps) treats roots of Dehn twists and tangential base points differently, not via this extension-subordinated fibration language.
missed.quote: on appelle $(\Pi,\mu)$-fibration (stricte) de groupoïdes subordonnée à l'extension (13), une hom. de groupoïdes (16) $f : C' \to C$
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This gives a clean groupoid-theoretic packaging of 'fractional' braid/twist symmetries (e.g. square roots of Dehn twists for hyperelliptic or level structures), which matters when building towers of Teichmüller groupoids. Its interest is modest: it is essentially standard gerbe/2-group equivariance.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is a routine (if neatly formulated) gerbe-type statement: a fibre is the action groupoid of the extension group on a torsor. The general definition is an unfinished draft of μ-equivariant central extensions of groupoids. It is historically interesting as part of Grothendieck's Teichmüller groupoid program but not a hidden result.
transcription_corrections: In (15) the right-hand side is ℰ(ℰ_ξ), with a script/calligraphic ℰ applied to the torsor ℰ_ξ; the transcription is right.
Line 'de façon générale... extension {+centrale+} de groupes [-commutatifs-]': the struck word over 'Π' looks like 'commutatifs', consistent with the transcription.
The bracket at the end reads approximately '[+ surjectivité dans (13) sur les objets, quitte à préciser]'; '(13)' is written '13)' at the line start.
Item 2°) is written above 1°) in the manuscript (added later), as transcribed; 'compatible avec les Π-op. internes' is an insertion replacing the struck 'de façon'.
